messages:
Alex (People Ops): Thanks for the all-hands Q&A — dropping this thread for any follow-ups on remote/hybrid travel, offsites, and workspace policies. I’ll answer what I can and loop in @Jordan (Office Ops) and @Sam as needed. Post questions here. :wave:

Priya (Engineering): Quick q — is there a required minimum in-office days per month for US remote employees?

Alex (People Ops): Short answer: no strict company-wide minimum. We recommend teams set norms (eg 1–2 days/month) and document them in the team handbook. Teams that do onboarding, client work, or have IRL collaboration goals may ask for more frequent presence. I’ll add a team-norms template later today.

Maya (PM): For the next company offsite — how do we handle travel modality? Train vs flight vs reimbursement caps?

Jordan (Office Ops): For domestic trips under ~6 hours we prefer train when practical. Reimbursements: standard economy for flights, standard rail fare for trains. If someone needs an upgrade for medical reasons or long-haul with a documented condition, submit to benefits@redwood.com. Internal booking link: https://redwood-ops/book-travel (internal).

Liam (People Ops): Can you clarify the home office stipend? Is it recurring or one-time? I recall a change last year.

Alex: It's a one-time $600 setup stipend for new hires (covers desk/chair/monitors). We also provide an internet stipend of $30/month for full-time remote employees. Contractors have different rules — managers should check the contractor policy doc.

Sam (CEO): Quick note from me — for the big company offsite in October the company will cover travel (economy), accommodation, and group meals for official days. Personal extras (upgrades, extra nights) are on you. We want to encourage in-person attendance but it’s not mandatory. If there’s a strong reason to miss (family, medical), please let your manager know. :thumbsup:

Priya (Engineering): If I’m traveling from EU to US for the offsite do we provide visa invitation letters or any travel support?

Jordan (Office Ops): Yes — Office Ops will provide invitation/visa support letters and coordinate. Please submit requests at least 6 weeks before travel using the internal visa form (/forms/visas) or DM me directly. We can also flag urgent cases.

Maya (PM): Are childcare or dependent-care reimbursements available for offsite days? Asking for parents on the team.

Liam (People Ops): We’re running a dependent-care reimbursement pilot for this offsite: up to $150/day for official offsite days (requires receipts). Submit to payroll@redwood.com within 30 days; People Ops will confirm eligibility per country.

Priya (Engineering): For in-office desks — is it first-come or can teams reserve desks? Some of us do partial weeks and need a consistent spot.

Jordan (Office Ops): We have 12 reservable desks per floor. Teams can reserve via the Office Portal > Book a Desk. Unreserved desks are first-come. I’ll post a 1-minute how-to animated gif in #eng to show the flow.

Alex (People Ops): Follow-up action items I’ll take: 1) Publish an updated travel + visa FAQ, 2) Upload the team norms template to the handbook, 3) Confirm dependent-care pilot details and add to the offsite FAQ. I’ll post links here once they’re live. Anything else folks want clarified?

Priya (Engineering): Can managers pre-approve a small list of exceptions (eg extended family travel days) so the payroll team knows in advance?

Liam (People Ops): Good call — managers can pre-approve exceptions. Please cc payroll@redwood.com and include dates + reason. We’ll add an exceptions workflow to the FAQ.

Sam (CEO): Thanks Alex, Jordan, and the ops folks. If anyone has sensitive edge cases (medical, visas, family emergencies) please DM @Liam or me and we’ll handle privately. Appreciate the questions — keeps the policies practical. :clap:

OfficeBot: Poll created — Preferred offsite window: Oct 5–8 vs Oct 12–15. Vote in #all-hands (poll closes in 72h).
